subject: physics
title: Light travels in a straight line — torches, corners and shadows

scenes.narration: Switch on a torch. Look at its beam — it is straight! Light always travels in a straight line. This is called rectilinear propagation.
A toy is hidden around a corner. Light from the toy travels in a straight line. It cannot bend around the corner to reach our eyes. So we cannot see the toy!
Clear glass is transparent: it lets almost all light through. Butter paper is translucent: it lets some light through. Wood is opaque: it lets no light through at all.
Now hold an opaque ball in front of the torch. The ball blocks the light, and a dark shadow forms on the wall behind it. A shadow needs three things: a light source, an opaque object and a screen.
This is a pinhole camera. It has a tiny hole. Rays from the top of the object go through the tiny hole in a straight line and land at the bottom. So the image is upside down — we call it inverted!

questions.prompt: Butter paper lets some light through. What kind of material is it?
hints: Some light passes — not all, not none.
questions.explanation: Translucent materials let some light through, like butter paper.

questions.prompt: The image in a pinhole camera is upside down.
hints: Think about where the rays from the top of the object land.
questions.explanation: Light travels in a straight line through the tiny hole, so the image is upside down (inverted).
